subject: Cosmetics company data breach affects 340,000 clients
posts:
Cybersecurity failure exposes 340,000 Napoleon Perdis customer records through third-party vendor Retail Express.
Evidence: Vendor cyber attack, 340k records leaked, delayed disclosure.
#CyberSecurity #DataBreach #Australia 🌐

Napoleon Perdis announced that a third-party vendor, Retail Express, suffered a cyber attack compromising 340,000 customer records from late 2025 to mid-2026, assuring customers that the system has been permanently shut down and secured.

Corporate outsourcing of sensitive personal data to insecure third-party platforms exposes hundreds of thousands to scams and identity theft, revealing systemic negligence masked as routine vendor containment.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.85) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Awakening into Destruction.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 4.2, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Napoleon Perdis: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Shifted blame to vendor.
- Retail Express: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Insecure third-party storage.
Napoleon Perdis notified 340,000 customers that a historical customer database stored by third-party vendor Retail Express was accessed by unauthorized actors for months before discovery.

The Poison:
Companies aggressively harvest extensive customer histories and personal data for marketing, yet disclaim responsibility when outsourced third-party servers inevitably suffer catastrophic security breaches.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a Logical plane error (HOW). The company frames the breach as an isolated technical glitch by a vendor rather than acknowledging the inherent danger of perpetual, unsecured data warehousing.

Social Physics Analysis:
Napoleon Perdis runs a smart selfish maneuver by outsourcing data risk while retaining marketing upside. Blaming the third-party vendor acts as a projective shield, deflecting accountability from lax corporate data collection policies onto external contractors.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
When you map the gap between corporate data collection promises and actual third-party security failures, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil.

The Unavoidable Truth: Outsourcing customer data storage multiplies vulnerability points across third-party supply chains.

The Unavoidable Lie: Shutting down a compromised system fully erases the leaked records already exposed on dark web markets.

Alethekanon:
Conveniently framing data breaches as external vendor failures allows corporations to continue harvesting personal information without bearing the true cost of security stewardship.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply unsettling for 340,000 everyday customers who trusted a cosmetics brand with their birth dates, addresses, and purchase histories, only to discover their most private details were left exposed for months.

Spirithekanon:
"The integrity of the upright guides them, but the unfaithful are destroyed by their duplicity." Proverbs 11:3 PASS
Shifting blame to third-party vendors while profiting from data harvesting violates fundamental stewardship.

Topic:Cyber Crime

Cosmetics brand Napoleon Perdis says it became aware of a breach in June. (Supplied)

Cosmetics company Napoleon Perdis has been hit by a data breach, affecting almost 340,000 customers.

In an email to customers, the company said it was informed in June that a third party it had used to store customer records, Retail Express, had been hit by a cyber attack.

"In August 2026, Retail Express confirmed the unauthorised party had access between November 2025 and June 2026, affecting approximately 339,055 customer records," the email said.

The brand was launched in Sydney in 1995 by makeup artist and businessman Napoleon Perdis. (AAP)

"The incident has been contained and the system permanently shut down."

Napoleon Perdis said the breach affected its customers from pre-June 2025.

The information accessed included customer names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses and purchase histories.

"This system did not hold your bank account or card details, or the password for your napoleonperdis.com account.

"Our current online store … was not affected."

Napoleon Perdis warned customers to be wary of scam calls or emails impersonating the company and advised them to monitor their bank transactions.

The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner has been notified.
